title: Open normal quotient actions and K-injective kernel models
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] on the small coherent profinite site [def-weil-size-convention]. For a profinite group $P$, write $\mathcal A_P(A)$ for internal $A$-modules with condensed $P$-action [def-sfb-condensed-action-module], and $\Gamma_P$ for sections fixed after every profinite base change. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories and K-injective total right derived functors [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Use the Grothendieck abelian structures of these action categories, in which forgetting actions creates kernels and cokernels and hence detects exactness, together with the exact action restrictions, exact trivial inflation and exact scalar restriction of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]. Inflation along any continuous homomorphism of profinite groups is additive and exact, and scalar restriction leaves the underlying sheaf kernels and sheaf-cokernels unchanged. Let $G,L$ be profinite groups, let $K\triangleleft G$ be open normal, and put $Q=G/K$. Write $T(M)=M^K$, with residual $Q\times L$-action, $U$ for forgetting this residual action, and $r=\operatorname{Res}_K$ for action restriction along $k\mapsto(k,1)$. All invariant inclusions and inflation adjunctions have the normalized transposes of [def-sfb-normal-invariant-comparison-data]: restrict codomain to invariants, with inverse given by composing the inclusion. The quotient $Q$ is finite discrete and its projection admits a continuous set section $s:Q\to G$. The fixed sections defining $T$ form an internal submodule with a well-defined residual condensed $Q\times L$-action, induced by any lifts through $(s,1_L)$. Quotient inflation is left adjoint to $T$ with the specified normalized transposes. On objects and maps there are identities $UT=\Gamma_K r$ and $\Gamma_{G\times L}=\Gamma_{Q\times L}T$, normalized by their invariant inclusions.

Restriction $r$, the functor $T$, and every full-invariants functor $\Gamma_P$ preserve K-injective complexes. Every complex in each action category admits a K-injective resolution. There is a natural isomorphism
$$\beta:D(U)RT\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_KD(r).$$
For every K-injective resolution $i:N\to I$, both sides of $\beta_N$ are represented by the identical complex $U(TI)=(rI)^K$, and $\beta_N$ is its identity under the canonical resolution identifications. This normalization is independent of the resolution and applies to all unbounded derived objects.

proof.text: Since $K$ is open, every coset is open and the quotient topology on $Q$ is discrete. The cosets cover the compact space $G$, so finitely many cover it; hence $Q$ is finite. Choose one representative $s(q)$ in each coset. Every map from this finite discrete space is continuous, and the quotient projection composed with $s$ is the identity. Also $K$ is closed, since its complement is a union of open cosets, so it is a profinite group.

proof.text: Define $T(M)(S)$ to be the submodule of sections fixed by all $C(V,K)$ after every $V\to S$, as specified in [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. This condition is linear and stable under restriction. Compatible fixed sections glue in $M$; after any $V\to S$, their pullbacks cover $V$, and equality with each kernel translate holds on that cover and hence globally by separatedness. Thus it is a sheaf submodule. For $(q,l)\in C(S,Q\times L)$ act by $(s\circ q,l)$ on these sections. This preserves fixedness because $K\times1$ is normal in $G\times L$: for $k\in C(V,K)$ and a lift $g$, $k(gm)=g((g^{-1}kg)m)=gm$. Two lifts differ by a kernel-valued map, which acts identically on fixed sections; hence the action is independent of the section chosen. Products of lifts and lifts of products differ by such a map, proving the action law; a lift of the identity acts trivially. The formula commutes with pullbacks and is linear. Restrict an equivariant map to these submodules; identity, composition and sums restrict, so this defines the additive functor $T$.

proof.text: Write $F$ for quotient inflation. For $f:FX\to M$, equivariance gives $k f(x)=f(kx)=f(x)$ after every base change, since the kernel acts trivially on $FX$. Restrict its codomain to $T(M)$. It is $Q\times L$-equivariant by applying $f$ to any chosen lift. Conversely compose any $X\to T(M)$ with the invariant inclusion. These operations are inverse and commute with precomposition and postcomposition, giving $F\dashv T$ with exactly the normalized transposes of [def-sfb-normal-invariant-comparison-data]. Forgetting the residual action gives the very same fixed submodule as $\Gamma_Kr$, on maps as well. A fully fixed section of $M$ is fixed by $K$ and by every quotient lift; conversely a $K$-fixed section fixed by quotient lifts is fixed by every $(g,l)$, since $(g,l)$ differs from its chosen quotient lift by an element of $K\times1$. Thus $\Gamma_{G\times L}=\Gamma_{Q\times L}T$. The inclusions in both identities are the identical inclusions into $M$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-condensed-split-coset-induction] to $P=G\times L$ and $H=K\times1$, identifying $H$ with $K$. This is a closed subgroup. The continuous map $(g,l)\mapsto(gK,l)$ is constant precisely on the cosets $(g,l)H$, so the quotient topology gives a continuous bijection $P/H\to Q\times L$. Its inverse $(q,l)\mapsto(s(q),l)H$ is continuous, being the composite of the continuous representative map and the quotient projection. Thus $P/H$ is profinite, and its projection has the continuous section $(q,l)\mapsto(s(q),l)$. The cited lemma supplies an additive exact left adjoint to the actual restriction $r$. This application allows infinite $L$: it uses a split profinite coset projection, not finite index of $K\times1$.

proof.text: The categories are abelian and arbitrary action inflation is additive and exact by the structural hypotheses in the item (as supplied by [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]). The exact left adjoint to $r$ from step 4 and [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] imply that $r$ preserves K-injective complexes. The same lemma applied to $F\dashv T$ of step 3 proves preservation by $T$, since $F$ is exact. For every profinite $P$, trivial inflation is an additive exact left adjoint to full invariants with the stated transpose, by [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]; the same general lemma therefore proves that every $\Gamma_P$ preserves K-injectives.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective] to each action category: its Grothendieck abelian structure is part of the structural hypotheses, with the fixed size convention. This gives a K-injective resolution of every unbounded complex. By [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], for a resolution $i:N\to I$ the value $RT(N)$ is represented by $TI$. The exact action restriction in [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus] and its K-injective preservation from step 5 make $ri:rN\to rI$ a K-injective resolution. Consequently $R\Gamma_K D(r)(N)$ is represented by $\Gamma_K(rI)$. The same calculus states that forgetting actions is exact, so $D(U)RT(N)$ is represented by $U(TI)$. Step 3 identifies these as the identical complex, with identical differentials.

proof.text: For K-injective complexes $I,J$, every derived morphism between their localizations is represented by a unique homotopy class $h:I\to J$, by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. On this class both functors under comparison act by the same chain map $UT(h)=\Gamma_Kr(h)$, by step 3. Their identity comparison on each K-injective representative is therefore natural for all derived morphisms, not just morphisms initially given as maps of unresolved complexes. The computation isomorphisms of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] give the isomorphism $\beta:D(U)RT\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_KD(r)$, whose component on every such representative is the identity.

proof.text: For two K-injective resolutions $i:N\to I$ and $j:N\to J$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] with target $J$ to represent $Qj\,(Qi)^{-1}$ by a unique homotopy class $h:I\to J$. Its equation $Q(hi)=Qj$ implies $hi\simeq j$ by the same Hom bijection with source $N$ and target $J$. Represent the inverse derived map by $k:J\to I$; injectivity of the Hom bijections with targets $I,J$ gives $kh\simeq1_I$ and $hk\simeq1_J$. Applying the additive functors $UT$ and $\Gamma_Kr$ preserves these homotopies and gives the same maps by step 3. Hence their identity comparisons commute with all resolution identifications. This proves the normalization for every resolution and its independence of that resolution, without a bound on degrees.
